title: Choose the visual world for Tarun's portfolio
question: The roll assigned the Vintage Apple HIG Binder. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Apple HIG Binder
options.thesis: The developer portfolio as an authoritative system manual.
options.viewport: A ring-bound manual spread introducing the developer, structured exactly like an OS spec.
options.risk: Might feel too archival if the typography isn't razor-sharp.

raised.raise: The manual commands extreme focus by owning the entire viewport as one continuous printed spread.
Typographic alignment follows absolute, uncompromising grid discipline.

options.label: Aerospace Mission Control
options.thesis: A crash-free mobile portfolio visualized as a mission-critical telemetry dashboard.
options.viewport: A dense terminal dashboard tracking live app stability and project metrics.
options.risk: Can feel too chaotic if the information architecture isn't strict.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Crash-free stats and performance metrics visualized as physical ballistic needles.
options.viewport: A row of identical meters monitoring different domains of mobile development.
options.case: Fuses perfectly: mobile performance metrics map exactly to analog ballistics.
options.risk: Requires flawless canvas animation to feel authentic.

options.label: Brick Build Instructions
options.thesis: Building apps treated as step-by-step physical assembly.
options.viewport: Numbered exploded steps showing the developer's tech stack snapping together.
options.case: Very strong conceptual map to 'building' products.
options.risk: Might feel slightly too playful for enterprise clients.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard dark mode developer portfolio.
canonCard.viewport: A standard hero section with a bento box layout below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other developer portfolios.
